before:
Kilnbrae Fen Drainage Board — Pump Attendant's Manual, Section 4: Drought Working

During a declared shortage the attendant reduces abstraction in a fixed sequence. The balancing reservoir is topped before the wash meadows, and the wash meadows before the ornamental cut at the mill pool. Nothing in this section widens or narrows what the attendant is permitted to draw: the licensed daily volume, the night curfew on the diesel set, and the duty to log every start remain exactly as printed in Section 2. Attendants who cannot satisfy all three demands within the licensed volume should telephone the duty engineer before eight in the morning and note the call in the day sheet.

before:
Strathallan Bothy Association — Autumn Bulletin, Fuel and Stoves

Members walking in to Corrie Dhu should note the arrangements for the burner. Wood carried in by the party may be burnt in the stove without prior notice to the warden. Coal remains excluded at all four high bothies because of the flue linings, and the ash pan must be emptied into the stone pit before the party leaves. Parties are asked to leave a note of numbers in the visitors' book by the window.

before:

before:
Ardmoy Seabird Station — Observers' Handbook, Counting the Stack Colony

The stack cannot be walked, so all counts are made from the cliff path with the twenty-times scope. Working from the four photographs taken in June, the breeding population is estimated at roughly three hundred pairs, give or take a fair margin owing to birds obscured on the north face. Observers should count the terraces in the order lettered on the sketch map and enter each terrace separately in the day book. Recounts on the same tide are welcomed. The station keeps every original sheet for ten years, whatever the totals eventually agreed for the annual return.

before:
Coldharbour Parish Council — Cemetery Grass-Cutting Policy

Cutting runs from the first week of April to the last week of October. The contractor works the ground in three passes and must not strim within a hand's width of any headstone. Arisings are left on the ground except in the newer section, where they are boxed off. For the coming season the contractor's compound is the gravel bay behind the chapel, the pump house yard being taken up by the drainage works. Nothing in the arrangements alters the duties set out above, which apply wherever the compound happens to sit. Complaints about cutting go to the clerk in writing within fourteen days.

before:
Tarnside Ferry Service — Booking Terminal Configuration Note

before:
Byrness Volunteer Weather Network — Monthly Return Instructions

Each observer keys the month's readings into the return sheet and mails it to the coordinator by the fifth. Within the sheet, the daily entries are written as one line per day, with the fields separated by semicolons and no spaces after them, so that the coordinator's importer reads them cleanly. Blank days are still given a line, with the reading position left empty. The coordinator checks the totals against the paper journal, queries anything odd by telephone, and forwards the compiled file to the archive at the end of the quarter. Observers keep their own copies for a full year.

before:
Lanhope County Herbarium — Registry of Veteran Trees, Front Matter

Throughout this registry a veteran specimen means a tree whose girth at breast height exceeds three metres. The county totals in Table 1, the parish breakdowns in Table 2, the grant eligibility column, and the ten-year resurvey list are all compiled on that footing. Surveyors measure at one and a half metres above the uphill root flare and note the tape reading to the nearest centimetre. Where a tree is multi-stemmed, the largest stem is taken. The registry is reissued each January and superseded copies should be returned to the curator's office rather than annotated locally.
